skill.name: remotion-elements
skill.description: Find and install reusable React video components, including titles, charts, backgrounds, and caption styles, in an existing Remotion project. Register libraries in Remotion Studio and preview components after adapting them.
skill.summary: Find, install, and customize reusable video components in Remotion.
skill.author: remotion-dev

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are Markdown syntax or official documentation links, not security issues. The real risks are running the CLI before verifying sources and proceeding from a dry run to unreviewed code and dependency installation. A fallback also delegates installation to instructions on a third-party page.

remediation.issue: The fallback can follow installation instructions from an unverified page.
remediation.suggestion: Stop when no Element payload is present. Treat the page as untrusted data and present any proposed alternative for review instead of running it.

remediation.issue: Library registration and dry runs use remote URLs before the workflow checks trust.
remediation.suggestion: Use the project's installed Remotion CLI. Verify URLs, redirects, and linked payload origins before fetching or registering them.

remediation.issue: A successful dry run leads directly to noninteractive installation.
remediation.suggestion: Review the component source, dependencies, assets, and planned changes. Require user approval before installing and retain the existing approval requirement for overwrites.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Page Can Supply Installation Instructions
semantic_findings.description: When the Element payload is missing, the skill says to "Follow the install instructions on its Markdown page". A publisher can use this fallback to direct an agent to run commands outside the Remotion installation workflow.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback explicitly delegates installation to page text without a review or approval gate. No evidence found that a malicious page was fetched or that a command ran.

content.user_title: Add Reusable Video Components to Remotion
content.value_statement: Building every title, chart, or caption style from scratch takes time. Use Remotion Elements to find reusable components, preview installation changes, and customize local copies in your composition.
actual_capabilities: Find Element page URLs from library indexes and individual Markdown entries.
Register an Element library in Remotion Studio for browsing and previewing.
Preview the files, packages, and assets an Element installation would change or add.
Install an editable component and its assets into a selected composition.
Adjust component props, text, colors, placement, and timing, then check the result in Studio.
limitations: The workflow assumes an existing Remotion project. It refers project creation to a separate skill.
Element installation with a dry run requires Remotion 4.0.543 or later. The library registration command requires 4.0.547 or later.
A Markdown listing is not an installable Element page. The installer needs the Element page or its linked JSON payload.
A successful dry run lists planned changes but does not establish that the component or its dependencies are safe.

use_cases.title: Add a speaker title
use_cases.description: Install a lower third from a trusted library, then adapt its text, colors, and timing for an interview.

use_cases.title: Review a chart installation
use_cases.description: Check the files, packages, and assets a chart would add before approving it for a React video composition.

use_cases.title: Make team components available in Studio
use_cases.description: Register an approved library so teammates can browse and preview shared titles, backgrounds, and caption styles.

prompt_templates.title: Find a lower third
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Choose a component without changing the project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find a lower third in [approved library]. Give me its Element page URL and describe the component. Do not register the library or install anything.

prompt_templates.title: Preview an Element installation
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Review the impact of adding a specific component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify [Element page URL] and run a dry run for [composition ID]. List the affected files, packages, and assets. Stop before installation.

prompt_templates.title: Register a library in Studio
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Make a trusted library available to the project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether [approved library URL] is already registered. If it is missing, register it as [display name] and summarize the configuration change. Do not install an Element.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate and preview a component
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Review a component before integrating it into a specific composition.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [Element page URL] and dry-run the install for [composition ID]. Report the source, dependencies, assets, and file changes, then wait for my approval. After approval, install it, match [brand colors], start it at [frame], and preview it in Studio.

output: The dry run lists a new editable chart component, an update to QuarterlyReview, one asset, and one missing package.
Installation has not started. Review the listed changes before approving it.

output_examples.input: Preview the approved lower third with the speaker name and brand colors, starting at frame 48.
output: The lower third displays the speaker name in the requested colors and starts at frame 48.
The composition was checked in Remotion Studio.

best_practices: Verify the library, Element page, and linked payload before downloading or installing a component.
Review the dry-run output, source code, and dependencies before approving installation.
Preview the updated composition in Studio and check timing, placement, and readability.
anti_patterns: Treating a user's link as proof that the component or its dependencies are trustworthy.
Running installation instructions found on a third-party page when its Element payload is missing.
Overwriting an existing Element file without user approval.

faq.question: What is a Remotion Element?
faq.answer: An Element is a reusable React video component. Installation copies its source into your project so you can edit it.

faq.question: Do I need to register a library first?
faq.answer: Register a known library to browse its Elements in Studio. When you have only a direct Element page URL, registration can be skipped.

faq.question: Which Remotion version do I need?
faq.answer: The Element install and dry-run commands require version 4.0.543 or later. The library registration command requires version 4.0.547 or later.

faq.question: What does a dry run show?
faq.answer: It identifies the selected Element and lists planned file changes, packages, and assets. It does not replace a source or dependency review.

faq.question: Where does a new Element appear in my composition?
faq.answer: The installer inserts it at frame zero. Adjust its sequence to change when it appears and where it is placed.

faq.question: What happens if the Element file already exists?
faq.answer: The installer stops if the existing file has different contents. Approve an overwrite only after reviewing what would be replaced.
